memory.keep.note: Decision vocabulary. The product's Accept/Skip are immediate server actions; keep/drop/undecided name a local judgment that is only transmitted on Apply, which is a genuinely different thing.

memory.drop.note: Decision vocabulary, the counterpart to memory.keep. The product's Accept/Skip are immediate server actions; keep/drop/undecided name a local judgment that is only transmitted on Apply.

memory.undecided.note: Decision vocabulary: the third state, a claim the reviewer has not judged yet. The product has no such state — upstream a proposal is pending until an immediate Accept or Skip resolves it.

memory.applying.note: The commit's busy state. The catalog's reviewqueue.accepting ("Accepting...") speaks the server vocabulary, but this button commits a local keep/drop judgment and reads "Apply decided" at rest — the busy state must not switch vocabularies mid-press.

memory.dropped.note: Result of a commit, in the local vocabulary. The catalog's reviewqueue.skipped is "Proposals skipped" — Skip is the product's own immediate server action, while this count is the reviewer's drops the engine confirmed removed. Same number, our word for it.

memory.draftsWillApply.note: Apply-dock forecast. The dock used to say drafts "will be sent", a fourth verb for the commit beside keep/drop and Apply; the catalog only reports per draft after the fact ("Applied") and has no forward-looking phrase to borrow. Counts drafts, not claims.

memory.nearLimit.note: The product ships caps and a binary budget rejection, nothing for approaching one; extended from its "Limits:" label.

memory.overLimit.note: The product ships caps and a binary budget rejection, nothing for approaching one; extended from its "Limits:" label. This is the far side of memory.nearLimit.

memory.restorePoint.note: Restore-point framing over the product's existing backup export. The catalog offers the file operation (exportBackup) but never the pre-flight habit of taking one before a destructive batch.

memory.restorePointDone.note: Restore-point framing over the product's existing backup export; the confirmation half of memory.restorePoint. memorysettings.memoryBackupExported names the file, not the safety net.

memory.facetsComputed.note: Facet-rail provenance heading (the review study's grouping): a facet the console derives itself. The catalog has no facet rail and so nothing that groups fields by where they came from.

memory.facetsFromModel.note: Facet-rail provenance heading (the review study's grouping): a facet the extraction model asserted. See memory.facetsComputed for why the group names are ours.

memory.facetsYours.note: Facet-rail provenance heading (the review study's grouping): a facet the reviewer set by hand. See memory.facetsComputed for why the group names are ours.

memory.autoIncluded.note: Batch reporting: the product reports per draft; we report per batch. Plural-selected because the apply sheet lists this section from one row up — an earlier version only rendered it at two or more, on the grounds that a single dependency was reported inline on its own row, but the sheet is where the batch is accounted for and it cannot skip the first one.

memory.queueEmpty.note: Empty queue: the product has no string for this state (its own empty state names the Sources screen's condition).

memory.disposition.new.note: Disposition names: schema values the product computes but never labels. The catalog's "New" is a source-status chip in the sources workspace; this is one of a lowercase triad with merge and rewrite, and borrowing a capitalized word for one of three breaks the set.

memory.disposition.merge.note: Disposition names: schema values the product computes but never labels. `merge` folds new material into a memory that already exists.

memory.disposition.rewrite.note: Disposition names: schema values the product computes but never labels. `rewrite` replaces the stored section text instead of adding to it.

memory.nav.vault.note: Navigation label. The catalog names this view in full ("Memory Vault"); the console's own nav uses one word each so the four fit as equal targets on a phone without truncating. Owner's call, 2026-08-22 — the full catalog name still heads the screen.

memory.nav.review.note: The catalog's short navigation label happens to be exactly the one word the console's rail needs; the longer longtermmemorynavigation.reviewQueue still heads the screen itself.

memory.nav.activity.note: Navigation label. The catalog has an activityview namespace but no label for the view — upstream reaches it from a menu the console does not have. One word, per the memory.nav.vault rule.

memory.statetip.new.text: the source has not been imported yet
memory.statetip.new.note: Tooltip definition of the source state "New", in the memory.typetip.source shape — the catalog labels every source state but defines none of them, so all six meanings are ours.

memory.statetip.current.note: Tooltip definition of "Current". The catalog's sourcesworkspace.current is the bare label; the engine computes the state by comparing the source hash and extraction settings against the recorded fingerprint, which is what this says in words.

memory.statetip.sourceUpdated.text: the source text changed after extraction
memory.statetip.sourceUpdated.note: Tooltip definition of "Update available", naming which of the two inputs moved. The catalog's memoryvault.savedButRecallIsStale is the nearest sentence and is about the index, not the source.

memory.statetip.contextChanged.text: the text is unchanged; the scope or modes around it changed
memory.statetip.contextChanged.note: Tooltip definition of "Context changed", and the sentence that separates it from Update available — the two states are told apart only by which input moved, which no catalog string says.

memory.statetip.extractionIncomplete.text: the source was imported, but its extraction never finished
memory.statetip.extractionIncomplete.note: Tooltip definition of "Extraction incomplete". The catalog's sourcesworkspace.extractionDidNotFinish says the same in the label voice; this is the clause form, and it keeps the first half, because the state exists only on a source that HAS been imported and readers took the mark to mean the import failed.

memory.statetip.sourceMissing.note: Tooltip definition of "Source missing". The catalog's reviewqueue.sourceMissing labels it and sourcesworkspace.missingSourceMemory is an action button; neither says what the condition is.

memory.sourcesBlocked.note: Drafts held before review; the catalog says "blocked" only inside sentences and never as a label for the set of them. Also the per-row marker in the review queue, which is the same claim about one draft.

memory.sourcesReviewEach.note: The per-kind affordance for sources that must be curated, not bulk-imported. The catalog's verbs here are Import and extract / Re-extract / Select all / Refresh — all bulk, none for opting out of bulk.

memory.extractionText.note: The editable text extraction reads; the override is new to this console. Upstream extraction always reads the source note verbatim, so there is nothing to name.

memory.noMatchingSources.note: The catalog has the whole family — "No matching chats/characters/branches/personas/places" — but not sources, and the Sources search was borrowing the chats one while its own body text said "sources". Same sentence shape, right noun.

memory.zonePreview.note: Detail-pane zone label (v5), anchored to catalog vocabulary: "preview" from reviewqueue.evidenceAndPreview / previewUnavailable, where it only ever appears inside a longer phrase. Lowercase because eyebrows uppercase in CSS.

memory.zoneDiff.note: Detail-pane zone label (v5), built from reviewqueue.existingValue / proposedValue, which are whole interpolated sentences carrying the value. The arrow pairing them as one eyebrow is ours. Lowercase because eyebrows uppercase in CSS.

memory.zoneNewMemory.note: Detail-pane zone label (v5), from reviewqueue.newMemory. Kept lowercase because zone eyebrows uppercase in CSS and this same string also renders in the zone's foot line, which does not — the catalog's title-cased "New memory" would read as a heading there.

memory.zoneExtraction.note: Detail-pane zone label (v5), from the extractiondetails namespace. Lowercase for the same reason as memory.zonePreview; the catalog's "Extraction" is a settings-section heading, which is the one place this word is NOT an eyebrow.

memory.claim.note: The single reviewable item in the queue. The catalog has zero occurrences of "claim" in any key or value: the product's vocabulary is a five-word lifecycle — candidate (at extraction) → proposal / mutation (in review, inside a draft) → suggestion (once rejected) — and none of those five names the thing a reviewer holds one of. The console keeps "claim" because the wire schema already does: `claimKind: "static" | "change"` on interface Mutation (data.ts:40), so an object whose kind is a claimKind is a claim. ClaimDetail.tsx is named for that field and glossary.tsx anchors the term to it. Note "claim kind" itself is domain vocabulary, not a coinage — it names the schema field verbatim. Only the bare noun is ours.

memory.batch.note: The set of claims applied in one go, which may span drafts. Distinct from "draft", which is the container the engine returns claims in and which the catalog does have a word for. The product reports per draft; the console reports per batch, and the catalog has no word for the user's own apply-unit.

memory.section.note: The note sub-part. Unlike everything else here, the product DOES have a word for this and we are deliberately not using it: memoryvault renames the sub-part to "detail" user-visibly (memoryvault.addSection = "Create detail", newSection = "New detail", detailRequired, detailNameExample), so "detail" there really does mean the sub-part, not a detail pane. But the product contradicts itself: reviewqueue still says section (addToSection = "Add to section", updateSection = "Update section", sectionTextCannotBeEmpty). The schema and wire format do not contradict themselves at all — `sections: Record<string, NoteSection>`, mutation kinds `append_section` / `update_section`, `SECTION_CAP` (data.ts). The console keeps "section" because it matches the schema, the wire format, and one of the two product surfaces; memoryvault's "detail" is the outlier. Owner's call — recorded here so the divergence is a decision, not a drift.

memory.existing.note: Diff-zone eyebrow label, rendered on its own as well as inside memory.zoneDiff. Derived from reviewqueue.existingValue ("Existing: {{value}}"), a whole interpolated sentence carrying the value — it cannot be used as a bare label, so the catalog has no string for the label alone. Lowercase because eyebrows uppercase in CSS.

memory.proposed.note: Diff-zone eyebrow label, rendered on its own as well as inside memory.zoneDiff. Derived from reviewqueue.proposedValue ("Proposed: {{value}}"), a whole interpolated sentence carrying the value — it cannot be used as a bare label, so the catalog has no string for the label alone. Lowercase because eyebrows uppercase in CSS.

memory.noChanges.note: Toast after a save that found nothing to write, naming the action that found nothing rather than reporting a bare state. memoryvault.unchanged ("Unchanged") is a transfer-preview row status for one record; the console's own lorebooks.record.noChanges is the record editor's shorter form of the same idea.

memory.editing.note: Appended to a zone eyebrow while its textarea is open. The catalog has no editing MODE: upstream an edit is a form you open, so it names the verb (reviewEdit) but never the state a zone is in.

memory.editedTip.text: edited — you replaced this claim's proposed text; your version applies with the batch
memory.editedTip.note: Tooltip on the edited mark, on the row and in the detail alike — one fact, one sentence, per CHECKLIST §2. The catalog's reviewqueue.editedChange is a two-word noun phrase used inside longer server messages and explains nothing about when the edit lands.

memory.expand.note: Accessible name of a row's disclosure chevron. The catalog mentions expanding only inside a sentence about hidden conflicts and has no name for the control itself.

memory.collapse.note: Accessible name of a row's disclosure chevron when open; the counterpart to memory.expand. The catalog has no collapsible rows and so no word for closing one.

memory.stop.note: Halts a running import batch between sources. Upstream import is one request that either completes or is canceled by the transport (importCancelledSelectionRetained); there is no user-facing verb for stopping a batch part-way.

memory.save.autosaving.note: The review ledger's save pill. This was the coinage "Autosaving…", declined from the catalog on the grounds that a debounced ledger write is a different promise from a modal save the user pressed. Owner-overruled 2026-08-24: the distinction was not worth a coined word, and the longer string overflowed the phone dock's status row, which is the one place the pill has to fit.

memory.gloss.static.text: claim kind · an enduring fact or defined state — true about someone or the world, not established by a narrated event
memory.gloss.static.note: Definition of the schema value claimKind="static". The extractor prompt classifies claims this way and the wire format carries it, but the catalog never renders the value, so it has no definition for it.

memory.gloss.change.text: claim kind · an outcome caused by a specific event — traces back to a timeline event
memory.gloss.change.note: Definition of the schema value claimKind="change"; the counterpart to memory.gloss.static. The catalog's reviewqueue.dependentChange is about mutation dependencies, not about this field.

memory.gloss.new.text: disposition · creates a memory that does not exist yet
memory.gloss.new.note: Definition of the computed disposition "new" (see memory.disposition.new). The product computes the same three dispositions and labels none of them, so every definition in this triad is ours.

memory.gloss.merge.text: disposition · folds new material into a memory that already exists
memory.gloss.merge.note: Definition of the computed disposition "merge". The catalog's reviewqueue.mergeIntoMemory is a button that performs it; a button label is not a definition of the state.

memory.gloss.rewrite.text: disposition · replaces the stored section text instead of adding to it
memory.gloss.rewrite.note: Definition of the computed disposition "rewrite". The catalog's acceptReplacesSavedMemory says what accepting does, in the second person, at the moment of accepting — it cannot serve as the standing definition of a value.

memory.gloss.lowRisk.text: risk · the blast radius if this claim is wrong — low: additive and easy to undo
memory.gloss.lowRisk.note: Definition of the extractor's risk=low. The catalog renders the value (reviewqueue.riskLow "Low") but nowhere says what risk measures, and the whole point of the education pattern is that a rendered enum can explain itself.

memory.gloss.mediumRisk.text: risk · the blast radius if this claim is wrong — medium: worth a look before it lands
memory.gloss.mediumRisk.note: Definition of the extractor's risk=medium; see memory.gloss.lowRisk for why the catalog's bare value label cannot be reused as a definition.

memory.gloss.highRisk.text: risk · the blast radius if this claim is wrong — high: review this one
memory.gloss.highRisk.note: Definition of the extractor's risk=high; see memory.gloss.lowRisk for why the catalog's bare value label cannot be reused as a definition.

memory.optip.create_note.text: operation · create — makes a new memory (a script is the whole memory; a file is one section)
memory.optip.create_note.note: Definition of the mutation kind create_note, including the icon vocabulary it teaches. The catalog names the action (reviewqueue.createMemory) but never explains the op, and it has no icon family to explain.

memory.optip.append_section.text: operation · append — adds lines to the end of one section
memory.optip.append_section.note: Definition of the mutation kind append_section. reviewqueue.addToSection is the button; this is what the op does, which is what a reviewer holding an unfamiliar glyph needs.

memory.optip.update_section.text: operation · update — replaces one section's stored text
memory.optip.update_section.note: Definition of the mutation kind update_section, naming the one destructive op. reviewqueue.updateSection is the button label only.

memory.optip.add_link.text: operation · link — connects this memory to another memory
memory.optip.add_link.note: Definition of the mutation kind add_link. reviewqueue.addLink is the button label; memoryvault.explicitRelationshipsUsedToConnectThisMemoryToRelated explains the FIELD in the vault, not the review-time operation.

memory.optip.set_keywords.text: operation · keywords — replaces the memory's keyword list
memory.optip.set_keywords.note: Definition of the mutation kind set_keywords. The catalog's underTheHoodKeywords explains what keywords are for; it does not say that this op replaces the whole list rather than adding to it.

memory.optip.set_status.text: operation · status — changes the memory's lifecycle status
memory.optip.set_status.note: Definition of the mutation kind set_status. memoryvault.statusHelp explains the three statuses; this names the operation that writes one.

memory.optip.set_subjects.text: operation · subjects — changes who the memory is about
memory.optip.set_subjects.note: Definition of the mutation kind set_subjects. memoryvault.theCharacterOrRelationshipIdentitiesDescribedByThisMemory defines the field; this names the op.

memory.typetip.character.note: Definition of the note type "character". The catalog renders the type name as a vault filter heading (memoryvault.characters) and never says what belongs in one, which is what the type icon has to answer in place.

memory.typetip.relationship.text: memory type · relationship — the state between two people
memory.typetip.relationship.note: Definition of the note type "relationship". Its cardinality is the whole distinction from a character memory, and the catalog states it only as a save-time validation error.

memory.typetip.timeline_event.text: memory type · timeline event — something that happened, anchored in time
memory.typetip.timeline_event.note: Definition of the note type "timeline_event". The catalog has the plural heading (memoryvault.timelineEvents) and no definition; the time anchor is the part reviewers get wrong.

memory.typetip.thread.text: memory type · thread — an open question the story should resolve
memory.typetip.thread.note: Definition of the note type "thread". memoryvault.threads is a filter heading; nothing upstream says a thread is a question waiting on an answer.

memory.typetip.world.text: memory type · world — setting, places, rules
memory.typetip.world.note: Definition of the note type "world". memoryvault.world is the bare label; the three-word enumeration is what tells a reviewer whether a claim belongs here or in a scene.

memory.typetip.tone.text: memory type · tone — how scenes should feel
memory.typetip.tone.note: Definition of the note type "tone", the one type that is an instruction rather than a fact. memoryvault.tone is the bare label.

memory.typetip.source.text: memory type · source — an imported record that claims were extracted from
memory.typetip.source.note: Definition of the note type "source". The catalog's sourceNoteRecallHelp says a source note is audit evidence and is not recalled; this is the one-line form that fits a tooltip on an icon.

memory.typetip.scene.text: memory type · scene — one scene's record
memory.typetip.scene.note: Definition of the note type "scene". memoryvault.scenes is a filter heading with no definition behind it.

memory.flag.hasConflicts.note: Flag label and facet value: this claim disagrees with a stored field. The catalog's memoryvault.conflicts is a vault section heading listing them; a facet value has to be a predicate about a row, not the name of a panel.

memory.flag.conflictCount.one: {{count}} field conflict with the stored memory
memory.flag.conflictCount.other: {{count}} field conflicts with the stored memory
memory.flag.conflictCount.note: The has-conflicts flag as a sentence. The catalog's conflictsFound pair counts UNRESOLVED conflicts inside its own resolution UI, which the console does not have; ours counts fields that differ from the vault.

memory.flag.lowRisk.note: The extractor's risk value rendered as a phrase. The catalog renders the bare adjective (reviewqueue.riskLow "Low") beside a separate "risk |" label; the console renders one token, because it is a facet value and a chip, where a bare "Low" names nothing.

memory.flag.mediumRisk.note: The extractor's risk value rendered as a phrase; see memory.flag.lowRisk for why the catalog's split label and value cannot be reused.

memory.flag.highRisk.note: The extractor's risk value rendered as a phrase; see memory.flag.lowRisk for why the catalog's split label and value cannot be reused.

memory.flag.highRiskSentence.text: The extractor rates this claim high risk.
memory.flag.highRiskSentence.note: The high-risk flag as a sentence in the detail's signals zone, attributed to the extractor because risk is the model's own estimate and not a console judgment. The catalog states risk as a bare value and never attributes it.

memory.flag.mediumRiskSentence.text: The extractor rates this claim medium risk.
memory.flag.mediumRiskSentence.note: The medium-risk flag as a sentence; the counterpart to memory.flag.highRiskSentence, attributed for the same reason.

memory.flag.lowConfidence.note: Flag label and facet value for an extraction below the threshold. The catalog has the field (memoryvault.confidence) and the unit (reviewqueue.confidence "% confidence") but no name for the exception, because upstream never filters by it.

memory.flag.confidenceSentence.note: The low-confidence flag as a sentence, stating the measurement and the line it fell under. The catalog's confidenceHelp describes what confidence means; it has nothing that reports one claim against a threshold.

memory.flag.restatesVault.note: Flag label and facet value: this claim repeats a line already stored. The catalog filters near-duplicates out BEFORE review (underTheHoodDuplicates), so it has no word for one that survived and needs a human.

memory.flag.restatesSentence.text: Very similar ({{score}}) to a line already stored.
memory.flag.restatesSentence.note: The restates-vault flag as a sentence, carrying the similarity score so the reviewer can judge the match. Upstream never surfaces a similarity score at all.

memory.flag.duplicateIncoming.note: Flag label and facet value: two claims in this batch say the same thing. The catalog's extractionprompttemplates.duplicate is a template action ("Duplicate" a prompt) and its dedupe vocabulary describes work already done, never a pair still in front of you.

memory.flag.duplicateSentence.text: Very similar ({{score}}) to another incoming claim in this batch.
memory.flag.duplicateSentence.note: The duplicate-incoming flag as a sentence; the batch-internal counterpart to memory.flag.restatesSentence, and the reason the console needs a word for "batch" at all.

memory.flag.long.note: Flag label and facet value for an unusually large single contribution. The catalog rejects oversize SOURCES before extraction (rejectsASourceWhenItsEstimatedSizeExceedsThis) and caps section text, but has no signal for a claim that is merely big.

memory.flag.longSentence.text: Long entry: +{{chars}} chars in one claim.
memory.flag.longSentence.note: The long flag as a sentence, naming the contribution in characters because that is the unit the caps are written in.

memory.flag.undatedEvent.note: Flag label and facet value: a timeline_event whose text carries no date. The date convention is the console's own extraction contract; the catalog has timeline events but no rule about their text.

memory.flag.undatedSentence.text: A timeline event with no [YYYY-MM-DD] date in its text.
memory.flag.undatedSentence.note: The undated-event flag as a sentence, quoting the exact bracketed format the matcher looks for so the fix is unambiguous.

memory.flag.noKeywords.note: Flag label and facet value: a create with an empty keyword list. The catalog explains what keywords do (underTheHoodKeywords) and caps them, but never warns that a memory shipped without any.

memory.flag.noKeywordsSentence.text: A new memory with no keywords — keyword matching cannot find it.
memory.flag.noKeywordsSentence.note: The no-keywords flag as a sentence, naming the consequence rather than the condition, because the condition alone reads as a stylistic quibble.

memory.flag.keywordCapFull.note: Flag label and facet value: the memory this claim targets already holds the full 30 keywords, so the next one is refused. The catalog names this state only by rejecting a write after the fact (manualKeywordLimit), which is not a label a reviewer can read beforehand.

memory.flag.keywordCapFullSentence.text: The target memory has filled its {{cap}}-keyword cap — another keyword is refused.
memory.flag.keywordCapFullSentence.note: The at-cap keyword flag as a sentence. Interpolates the cap rather than spelling it, so the sentence cannot drift from KEYWORD_CAP the way the catalog's hardcoded "at most 30" would, and names the consequence because "at the cap" alone does not say the next write fails.

memory.flag.sectionNearCap.text: The section is close to its cap.
memory.flag.sectionNearCap.note: Section-pressure flag when no single section can be named (nothing projected). The catalog has no pressure model at all: upstream a write either fits or is rejected, so approaching a cap is a state it cannot describe.

memory.flag.sectionOverCap.text: The section would exceed its cap after this batch.
memory.flag.sectionOverCap.note: Section-pressure flag when no single section can be named; the far side of memory.flag.sectionNearCap. "After this batch" is the console's own projection over everything kept, which upstream does not compute.

memory.flag.sectionNearCapNamed.text: §{{key}} is at {{pct}}% of its {{cap}}-char cap after this batch
memory.flag.sectionNearCapNamed.note: Section-pressure flag naming the worst section. §key is the console's section typography; the projection over the whole batch has no upstream equivalent.

memory.flag.sectionOverCapNamed.text: §{{key}} would reach {{pct}}% of its {{cap}}-char cap after this batch — over the limit
memory.flag.sectionOverCapNamed.note: Section-pressure flag naming the worst section when the projection breaks the cap; the far side of memory.flag.sectionNearCapNamed, ending in the console's own memory.overLimit phrase.

memory.error.storageCap.title.text: A note hit a storage cap
memory.error.storageCap.title.note: Apply-failure class: the engine refused a write for exceeding a storage contract. The catalog reports the raw server message and has no taxonomy of apply failures, because upstream accepts one draft at a time and shows the error inline.

memory.error.storageCap.fix.text: Open the target note in the Memory Vault and prune the named field (Dedupe lines helps), then retry. Failed drafts stay pending — nothing was lost.
memory.error.storageCap.fix.note: The fix for memory.error.storageCap. Names a console-only affordance (Dedupe lines) and states the recovery guarantee; the catalog's recommendedFix family is about rejected extraction candidates, not about apply.

memory.error.draftMoved.title.note: Apply-failure class: the draft is no longer pending. The catalog has the server states (reviewqueue.notPending, superseded) as bare status words, not as a failure a reviewer has to act on.

memory.error.draftMoved.fix.text: Refresh — it is probably already resolved.
memory.error.draftMoved.fix.note: The fix for memory.error.draftMoved. Uses Refresh, one of the console's two reload words, because the queue is re-fetched rather than the failed action re-tried.

memory.error.sourceChanged.title.note: Apply-failure class: the draft's extraction context no longer matches its source. The catalog names the state (sourcesworkspace.contextChanged) as a source-row chip, never as the reason an apply failed.

memory.error.sourceChanged.fix.text: Re-extract the source, then review the new draft.
memory.error.sourceChanged.fix.note: The fix for memory.error.sourceChanged, in the catalog's own verb (sourcesworkspace.reExtract). The two-step sentence is ours because upstream re-extraction is offered on the source row, not as recovery from a failure.

memory.error.editRejected.title.note: Apply-failure class: the engine refused an editedMutation. The catalog validates edited mutations before accepting (invalidEditedMutation) and so has no name for one that failed at apply.

memory.error.editRejected.fix.text: Open the claim, revert or fix the edit, then retry.
memory.error.editRejected.fix.note: The fix for memory.error.editRejected. Offers reverting as well as fixing, which only makes sense where an edit is staged locally and can be dropped — a console-only state.

memory.error.upstream.title.note: Apply-failure class: a transport or 5xx failure. The catalog's errors.interfaceStopped treats a failed request as terminal; the console classifies it as retryable, which needs its own name.

memory.error.upstream.fix.text: Safe to retry — each mutation applies at most once.
memory.error.upstream.fix.note: The fix for memory.error.upstream, promising idempotency. The catalog never makes this promise (its retry strings only say a retry is or is not needed), and it is the whole reason this class is safe to retry unattended.

memory.error.applyFailed.note: The unclassified apply failure, and the heading of the failure card. The catalog's draftActionFailed carries the raw message; the console splits title from fix, so it needs a title for the case where there is no known fix.

memory.apply.failedCount.note: The failure tail of the apply toast, appended only when something failed. The catalog reports failures per draft inside batchResultSummary; the console reports once per batch, so the clause has to stand alone.

memory.toast.undid.note: Confirms an undo of a decision-ledger change, naming what was undone. The catalog has the button (memoryvault.undo) and failure (archiveUndoFailed) but no confirmation, because it has no undo stack to walk.

memory.index.rebuilding.note: Busy state of the recall-index rebuild button. The catalog names the phase (activityview.phaseRebuild) and the outcome (reindexComplete) but never the in-flight state, because upstream runs the repair from a settings screen that blocks.

memory.index.unhealthy.text: Recall index is {{state}} — saved memories may not be searchable.
memory.index.unhealthy.note: Banner when the engine reports an index health other than healthy. The catalog's semanticRecallUnavailable covers one cause and one consequence; this reports whatever state the engine names, and the consequence is the broader one.

memory.index.noEmbeddings.text: Semantic recall is unavailable on this engine (no embedding model) — retrieval runs on keywords and text matching only.
memory.index.noEmbeddings.note: Banner when the engine has no embedding model at all. The catalog's semanticRecallUnavailable blames a repairable index; this condition is not repairable and saying so would send the reviewer to a rebuild that cannot help.

memory.peek.rawMemory.note: Label of the peek's raw-JSON disclosure. The catalog's activityview.copyJson and technicalDetails belong to the debug log and name a copy action, not a fold holding one memory's stored record.

memory.peek.id.note: Accessible name for the copy control on the peek's id footer, phrased as the object being copied because the control's own verb is supplied by the shared component. The catalog never exposes a note id as a labeled, copyable field.

memory.backToQueue.note: Accessible name of the stacked detail's back button, in the catalog's own "Back to {destination}" shape (longtermmemorydetail.backToAgents). The destination is the console's own review list, which upstream has no stacked navigation for.

memory.backToVault.note: Accessible name of the stacked editor's back button; same shape and same reason as memory.backToQueue.

memory.review.groupBy.note: Accessible name of the grouping chooser, in the shape of the catalog's own memoryvault.sortBy. The product's review queue is one flat list with no grouping, so there is nothing to borrow.

memory.review.filter.note: Key half of the mobile three-button rail. The catalog has clearFilters and "active filters" prose but no bare noun for the control, because upstream filtering is a row of always-visible selects rather than one button.

memory.review.group.note: Key half of the mobile three-button rail; the control that opens memory.review.groupBy. See memory.review.filter for why the rail's three keys are ours.

memory.review.sort.note: Key half of the mobile three-button rail. The catalog's memoryvault.sortBy is the full phrase and does not fit a fixed 108px key column beside Filter and Group.

memory.review.decided.note: Label of the tally meter over keep/drop. The catalog's progress vocabulary is "reviewed / remaining" (reviewSummary), which counts server actions taken; decided counts local judgments not yet transmitted. Lowercase because the meter label uppercases in CSS.

memory.review.decidedOf.note: Accessible name of a group's tally bar, giving the bar's proportion as a number for screen readers. The catalog's reviewProgress is a whole status line, not a per-group figure.

memory.review.shownOf.note: How many rows survive the active facets, shown beside the bulk actions so a bulk press states its own blast radius. The catalog's memoryvault.shown is the bare word used inside a longer count phrase.

memory.review.chipDupes.note: Quick chip for the duplicate-incoming flag, clipped to one short word for the same reason as memory.review.chipRestates. The catalog's dedupe vocabulary is always the full word and always about work already done.

memory.review.keepShown.note: Bulk-decide the filtered set to keep. The catalog's bulk verbs act on a SELECTION (selectAll, skipSelected); the console has no selection here — the filter is the selection, which is what "shown" names.

memory.review.dropShown.note: Bulk-decide the filtered set to drop; the counterpart to memory.review.keepShown, and drop rather than skip because the decision is local until Apply.

memory.review.reset.note: Returns the filtered rows to undecided. The catalog has no third decision state to return to, so it has no verb for clearing a judgment; extractionprompttemplates.resetToDefault resets a template, not a decision.

memory.review.keepUndecided.note: Tooltip on a group's keep-all button, stating how many rows it touches and that decided rows are left alone. The catalog's bulk actions never exclude already-actioned rows, because upstream an actioned proposal leaves the queue.

memory.review.dropUndecided.note: Tooltip on a group's drop-all button; the counterpart to memory.review.keepUndecided.

memory.review.keepAllUndecidedIn.note: Accessible name of a group's keep-all button, naming the group because the visible tooltip cannot. The catalog has no grouped queue and so no per-group bulk action to name.

memory.review.dropAllUndecidedIn.note: Accessible name of a group's drop-all button; the counterpart to memory.review.keepAllUndecidedIn.

memory.review.clearDecisions.note: Group kebab item returning that group's decided rows to undecided. The catalog's memoryvault.clearFilters clears a view; there is no upstream state that clearing a decision could mean.

memory.review.decisionCycle.note: Accessible name of the row's tri-state decision control, stating the current value and the gesture. Upstream a proposal has two immediate buttons and nothing that cycles, so both halves are ours.

memory.review.claimPosition.note: Heads the stacked detail with the reviewer's position in the filtered queue rather than the target's title, because position is what j/k triage needs. The catalog's queue has no cursor and no position.

memory.review.noClaimOpen.note: Empty state of the desktop detail pane. The catalog's memoryvault.openAMemoryForDetailsOrAddOne is the vault's equivalent and offers a create the review queue cannot do.

memory.review.triageHint.text: j/k to move · a keep · d drop · Enter opens
memory.review.triageHint.note: Teaches the triage keys where the empty detail pane would otherwise be blank. The product binds no keys at all, so no part of this can trace.

memory.review.noMatch.text: No proposals match the active facets.
memory.review.noMatch.note: Empty state when facets filter everything away, in the catalog's own "No {nouns} match…" shape (memoryvault.noMemoriesMatchTheseFilters). The nouns are proposals and facets, and the catalog has no facets.

memory.review.noFacetValues.text: No facet values in this slice.
memory.review.noFacetValues.note: Empty state inside the facet drawer itself, when the other active facets leave nothing to offer. The product has no facet drawer, so it cannot have an empty one.

memory.apply.buttonShortChecking.note: The short apply button while preflight is in flight. memory.apply.buttonChecking is the same state for the long label, and exists for the same reason: eliding only the number keeps the button from changing width or vocabulary mid-press. A short button falling back to the long checking label defeats that — it grew and flashed the other wording on every decision.

memory.dock.detailTitle.note: Title of the sheet behind the dock's tally, which explains figures the dock can only state. The catalog has no equivalent because it applies one draft at a time from a modal and never has a mixed set to account for.

memory.dock.unitMutations.note: The same, for what the engine will actually write. memory.dock.ready calls this "ready", which says the state and not the unit; a reader comparing it to drafts and claims needs the unit.

memory.apply.buttonShort.note: The apply button on a phone, where the labelled form does not fit: measured at 390px the dock's counts want 221px and memory.apply.button another 159, against 366px of usable row. The catalog's bare "Apply" is the activity log's phase name and carries no count — and the count is the whole point of this button, which states how much a press is about to send. Dropping to the bare verb would leave the blast radius unstated on the one projection where the row is too tight to state it twice.

memory.review.view.note: Title of the sheet holding both arrangement questions — how the queue is divided and how it is ordered. The catalog splits these across memoryvault.sortBy and its own grouping controls and never names the pair, because upstream has no surface that asks both at once.

memory.review.anyFlag.note: The filter that keeps every claim carrying at least one quality flag, whichever flag it is. The catalog names individual flags but has no filter over the set, because upstream never computes the set.

memory.review.anySource.note: Summary beside the source filter when it is unnarrowed. Parallel to memory.review.anyOfFlags; the source count is not stated here because the row already carries it.

memory.review.moreFilters.note: Opens the facets held back from the sheet's first screen. DESIGN.md §4 puts the long tail behind a disclosure; the catalog's extractiondetails.advancedExtractionDetails is about extraction internals, not about a filter surface having more of itself.

memory.review.fewerFilters.note: The same disclosure once open. Named for what pressing it does rather than a bare chevron, so the control reads the same way in both states.

memory.review.activeCount.note: How many filter values are currently narrowing the queue, shown in the filter sheet's head. The catalog's extractionprompttemplates.activeTemplate marks one template as in force; this counts selections, which upstream has no multi-select facet to count.

memory.review.noneActive.note: The same slot when nothing is selected. A separate string rather than "0 active" because a zero count reads as a measurement and this is the absence of one.

memory.review.shownClaims.note: The filter sheet's running result, so a selection states its own effect before the sheet is dismissed. memory.review.shownOf is the bare ratio used where the noun is already on screen; here the list is behind a scrim and the noun has to come along.

memory.review.sortFlipHint.text: Tap the active sort again to flip direction.
memory.review.sortFlipHint.note: Help line under the sort options, where the same row both selects a sort and reverses it. The catalog has no reversible sort control and so no sentence explaining one.

memory.review.refreshQueue.note: Accessible name of the queue's re-fetch button. The catalog's activityview.refresh is the bare verb for the activity log; naming the object matters here because the header also carries a Retry for the save ledger.

memory.review.generatedAt.note: When the engine built the review payload now on screen. The catalog's memoryvault.generated marks a FIELD as model-generated; this is a timestamp on a snapshot, which upstream never shows because it never caches one.

memory.review.dedupedUpstream.note: How many candidates the engine dropped as near-duplicates before the console saw them. The catalog reports deduplications inside an extraction-details accounting line; here it is a one-clause footnote on the queue's provenance.

memory.review.willBeCreated.note: Accessible name of the green dot marking a target that does not exist yet. The catalog's reviewqueue.createMemory is the action; this marks a target as not-yet-real, which only matters where several claims share one pending target.

memory.review.capPct.note: The compact cap signal on a group header, where only the percentage fits. The catalog has no cap-pressure signal at all; activityview.limits ("Limits:") is a debug heading. Lowercase because the chip's row is data type, not a sentence.

memory.review.capTitle.text: §{{key}}: stored {{stored}} ch, {{projected}} after this batch, cap {{cap}}
memory.review.capTitle.note: The full numbers behind memory.review.capPct, on hover. Stored-versus-projected is the console's own batch projection and has no upstream equivalent.

memory.review.blockedDrafts.note: Heads an obligation card: drafts the engine will not accept until their reason is cleared. The catalog's reviewqueue.blockedMutations counts blocked MUTATIONS inside a longer server sentence; this counts the drafts holding them.

memory.review.claimsHeld.note: The second half of the obligation card's count line: how many claims sit inside the blocked drafts. "Held" rather than blocked, because the claims themselves are fine — their draft is not.

memory.review.claimCount.note: Bare count of claims under one blocked source. The catalog counts mutations (reviewqueue.mutations) — the wire word — where the console counts claims, which is the word the reviewer holds one of.

memory.review.extractingProgress.note: Busy label while re-extracting blocked sources one at a time, carrying an n/total. The catalog's savingAndExtracting states a total only, because upstream sends the batch in one request and cannot report progress through it.

memory.review.reextractNote.text: Re-extracting calls the model once per source and replaces each blocked draft with a fresh one.
memory.review.reextractNote.note: States the cost and the consequence before a bulk re-extract. The catalog's refreshExplanation makes the opposite promise (refresh does NOT call the model); there is no upstream sentence for what re-extraction spends.

memory.review.rawSummary.note: Fold holding the server's verbatim error text under a classified failure. The catalog's activityview.technicalDetails names the same idea in the debug log; here it sits inside a failure card where "technical details" would outweigh the fix above it.

memory.apply.button.note: The commit. The catalog's applyPreflighted ("Apply preflighted ({{count}})") names the server's preflight; this button applies the reviewer's decided set, which is the local ledger, and the count is drops plus ready keeps.

memory.apply.buttonChecking.note: The commit button while preflight is still in flight and the count is not yet known. Holding the label and eliding only the number keeps the button from changing width or vocabulary mid-press; the catalog has no debounced preflight to wait on.

memory.apply.progress.note: The commit button while applying, counting drafts. The catalog's reviewqueue.accepting ("Accepting...") speaks the server vocabulary and reports no progress, because upstream accepts one draft per press.

memory.apply.progressDraft.note: The same progress in the dock, where there is room to name the unit being counted. Drafts, not claims: one apply may span several drafts, which is why the console needed the word batch.

memory.dock.blocked.note: Preflight's blocked count in the dock; the counterpart to memory.dock.ready. reviewqueue.blockedMutations ("; {{count}} blocked before Apply") is a fragment welded to a server summary, punctuation and all.

memory.dock.checking.note: The dock while preflight is debounced or in flight. The catalog's preflight strings are all results; upstream preflight is an explicit button press, so there is no waiting state to name.

memory.detail.field.note: Fallback name for a conflicting field the engine did not name. The catalog's conflict strings always carry the field's own label; there is no word for the anonymous case. Lowercase because the eyebrow uppercases in CSS.

memory.detail.wholeMemory.note: Toggle that re-renders the preview with every section of the target present and the change marked in place. memoryvault.thisMemory names the memory; nothing upstream offers a scope toggle over a preview, because upstream previews one section.

memory.detail.appliesWithBatch.note: Note beside save/discard while editing, saying when the edit reaches the engine. Upstream an edited mutation is saved by the same press that accepts it, so there is no interval to explain.

memory.detail.editStaged.text: Edit staged — applies with the batch
memory.detail.editStaged.note: Toast confirming a staged edit. "Staged" is the console's word for a change held in the local ledger; the catalog's save confirmations (memorySaved) all mean the engine has it.

memory.detail.pendingInBatch.note: Chip marking a link target that does not exist yet but is created by another claim in the same apply. The catalog resolves link targets against saved memories only, so a target that exists only inside a batch is unnameable there.

memory.detail.earlierLines.note: Fold holding the stored lines above an append's context window. The catalog folds hidden CONFLICTS (moreConflicts) and nothing else; it has no line-level view of a section.

memory.detail.moreLines.note: Fold holding the rest of an inlined memory shown as context. Same reason as memory.detail.earlierLines: the product has no line-level rendering of stored text.

memory.detail.unchangedLines.note: Fold collapsing an unchanged run inside a diff. memoryvault.unchanged is a transfer-preview row status for a whole record; this counts lines inside one section's diff, which upstream never renders.

memory.detail.showRest.note: Fold holding the tail of a new memory's section. The catalog's reviewqueue.showAll is the bare verb over a list; this names how much text is behind the fold, which is the number that decides whether to open it.

memory.detail.keywordCount.note: How full the keyword list is after this claim, against the product's own 30-keyword cap. The catalog states the cap only when refusing a write (manualKeywordLimit).

memory.detail.capAfterBatch.note: Section pressure in the zone foot, rounded to thousands because it sits beside a character delta. "After batch" is the console's projection over everything kept; the product has no such projection.

memory.detail.belowThreshold.note: The clause appended to the extraction-confidence line when it fell short. Read on its own it is a fragment; it is registered as one because the sentence before it is a catalog mirror carrying the number.

memory.headline.create.note: Claim headline for create_note. The catalog's reviewqueue.createMemory is a button; a headline states what the claim does to which memory, and the word order around the type and the reference is locked to English, so it is one string with slots.

memory.headline.append.note: Claim headline for append_section, shaped after the catalog's reviewqueue.addToSection but carrying the section and the target, which the button label cannot. One string with slots, so the word order stays translatable.

memory.headline.update.note: Claim headline for update_section. "Rewrites" rather than the catalog's "Update section", because this is the one destructive op and the headline is where a reviewer decides whether to read the diff below it.

memory.headline.link.note: Claim headline for add_link, with both ends of the link as slots. reviewqueue.addLink is the bare button; a link headline is meaningless without naming what it joins.

memory.headline.keywords.note: Claim headline for set_keywords, in the catalog's own verb (replaceKeywords) with the target named. "Replaces" is load-bearing: the op discards the existing list rather than adding to it.

memory.headline.status.note: Claim headline for set_status, from the catalog's reviewqueue.changeStatus with the target named.

memory.headline.subjects.note: Claim headline for set_subjects, from the catalog's reviewqueue.updateSubjects with the target named. Kept parallel with memory.headline.status so the seven headlines read as one set.

memory.zoneEditing.note: Zone eyebrow while the preview is a textarea, naming what is being edited so it is clear the stored text is not. The catalog's reviewEdit is the verb on a button; there is no upstream edit mode to label. Lowercase because eyebrows uppercase in CSS.

memory.vault.id.note: Key in the editor's key/value header. The catalog never exposes a note id as a labeled field — upstream ids live in diagnostics — so the one word this column needs has no source. Lowercase to match the column, whose other keys are catalog words rendered lowercase.

memory.vault.type.note: Key in the editor's key/value header. memoryvault.type is "Type", a filter heading in a vault that titles its controls; this column runs lowercase keys against their values, and a capital here would be the only one in the run.

memory.vault.status.note: Key in the editor's key/value header, over the three status buttons. Declines memoryvault.status ("Status") for the same reason as memory.vault.type: the column is lowercase, and the capital form is still used as the button group's accessible name.

memory.vault.keywords.note: Key in the editor's key/value header, over the memory's effective keywords. Declines memoryvault.keywords ("Keywords") for the same reason as memory.vault.type; the words are the catalog's, only the case is the column's.

memory.vault.links.note: Key in the editor's key/value header, over the memory's outgoing links. memoryvault.linkedMemories names a whole panel and memoryvault.link is the singular action; neither is the plural noun this column needs. Lowercase to match the column.

memory.vault.noneOpen.note: Empty state of the desktop editor pane. memoryvault.openAMemoryForDetailsOrAddOne is the closest and offers a create the console's vault does not have.

memory.vault.selectToEdit.text: Select a memory to edit it.
memory.vault.selectToEdit.note: Body of memory.vault.noneOpen, in the catalog's own "Select a {noun} to {verb}" shape (selectALorebookToInspectItsEntries). The noun and the verb are both different, and the console's vault edits rather than inspects.

memory.vault.dedupeLines.note: Drops near-duplicate lines inside one section's text. The catalog dedupes CANDIDATES during extraction (extractiondetails.deduplications) and never offers it as an edit over stored text.

memory.vault.noDupeLines.note: Result of memory.vault.dedupeLines when nothing matched. The catalog reports deduplication only as a count inside an extraction accounting line, so it has no null result to borrow.

memory.vault.dedupeResult.one: Dropped {{count}} near-duplicate line · {{chars}} ch freed — save to keep it
memory.vault.dedupeResult.other: Dropped {{count}} near-duplicate lines · {{chars}} ch freed — save to keep it
memory.vault.dedupeResult.note: Result of memory.vault.dedupeLines, stating what it removed, what that bought, and that the change is still a draft. The last clause is the important one and has no upstream equivalent, because upstream nothing edits stored text in place.

memory.vault.archived.note: Toast confirming an archive, naming the memory because the row it came from may have left the view. The catalog's archiveSuccess pair counts memories ("{{count}} memories archived.") for a multi-select the console does not have.

memory.vault.archiveWithExtracted.note: The second of the vault editor's two archive controls: the first archives this memory, this one archives it together with the memories extracted from it. The catalog's own archive labels are all single-scope (memoryvault.archive) or speak about a multi-select (sourceoperation.applyArchive, "Archive selected records"), and it names the cascade only as a delete (sourcesworkspace.deleteExtractedMemoriesTitle). "extracted memories" is the catalog's word for the set.

memory.vault.archiveWithExtractedConfirm.text: Archive {{title}} and any memories extracted from it? Archiving excludes them from recall without deleting them.
memory.vault.archiveWithExtractedConfirm.note: Confirm before the cascading archive. The catalog's confirmArchive counts a multi-select ("Archive the source and {{count}} selected linked memories?") and its delete confirms all promise permanence, which this action does not have. The second sentence exists because the control it replaced claimed the opposite; it restates statusHelp's "archived memories cannot" be recalled for a reader who is mid-decision.

memory.vault.archivedWithExtracted.one: Archived {{title}} and {{count}} memory extracted from it
memory.vault.archivedWithExtracted.other: Archived {{title}} and {{count}} memories extracted from it
memory.vault.archivedWithExtracted.note: Toast after the cascading archive, naming the memory for the same reason as memory.vault.archived and reporting how far the cascade reached. The catalog's archiveSuccess pair is a bare count ("{{count}} memories archived.") with no target to attribute them to.

memory.sources.search.note: Accessible name of the sources search field, in the catalog's own "Search {nouns}" family (searchMemories, searchChats, searchStatuses). The family has no sources member, which is the same gap memory.noMatchingSources fills.

memory.sources.confirmImport.note: Accessible name of the above-threshold confirm dialog. The catalog confirms deletes and archives but never an import, because upstream an import spends nothing until extraction is chosen separately.

memory.sources.oneModelCall.note: States the price of the batch in the confirm, beside the catalog's own savingAndExtracting. The catalog never quantifies extraction cost; this console asks before spending it, so it has to.

memory.sources.perSourceDetail.note: Fold holding the import report's per-source table. The catalog's importResultSummary is one flat sentence of totals with no breakdown to fold.

memory.sources.reportSummary.text: {{ok}} of {{total}} sources · {{kept}} proposed memories ready to review.
memory.sources.reportSummary.note: The import report's headline count. The catalog reports per source (sourceSavedProposalsReady) and, for a batch, only a machine-shaped totals line (importResultSummary); neither is a sentence for a person reading one card.

memory.sources.awaitReview.note: How many proposals an imported source is still holding. The catalog has only the negative (noProposedMemoriesAwaitReviewForSource); the positive form, and its count, are ours.

memory.sources.moreDerived.note: Fold over the memories a source produced, past the first three. The catalog's "{{count}} more" phrasings are all welded into sentences about hidden conflicts.

memory.sources.openInLorebooks.note: Accessible name of the jump from a lorebook source to the console's lorebook tool, in the catalog's own memoryvault.openInSources shape. The destination is a console tool the product does not have.

memory.sources.stopNote.text: Stop keeps the sources that have already finished and leaves the rest unprocessed.
memory.sources.stopNote.note: Says what memory.stop does before it is pressed. The catalog's importCancelledSelectionRetained explains a transport cancellation after the fact and promises the SELECTION is retained, which is a different promise.

memory.sources.stopped.note: The job dock after a stop, reporting what did land. The catalog's statusCancelled is a bare row status; there is no upstream partial-batch report because there is no upstream per-source loop.

memory.sources.searchEmpty.text: The search {{query}} matches nothing. Clearing it would show {{count}} sources.
memory.sources.searchEmpty.note: Empty state naming the search that emptied the list and what clearing it would restore. The catalog's empty states name the filter set (filteredEmptyDescription) but never say what removing it would show.

memory.sources.searchEmptyScoped.text: The search {{query}} matches nothing in {{scope}}. Clearing it would show {{count}} sources.
memory.sources.searchEmptyScoped.note: memory.sources.searchEmpty when an import scope is also narrowing the list, so the sentence names both constraints rather than blaming the search alone.

memory.sources.emptyScopedBody.text: Widening the import scope will show sources from other chats.
memory.sources.emptyScopedBody.note: Body under the catalog's noLorebooksAreAvailableInThisScope, naming the way out. The catalog states the condition and stops; it never tells the reader that the scope is the thing to change.

memory.sources.emptyReadyBody.text: New chat summaries appear here as they are written. An imported source returns when its text or scope changes.
memory.sources.emptyReadyBody.note: Body of the cleared-backlog empty state, saying why the screen will fill again. The second sentence is what makes the wider Ready to import view honest: it also refills from sources already imported, which the catalog's empty states never describe because upstream this view holds only new ones.

memory.sources.emptyImportedBody.text: Import a source to see it here.
memory.sources.emptyImportedBody.note: Body under the catalog's noSourcesHaveBeenImportedInThisScope, naming the action that fills the view. Same gap as memory.sources.emptyReadyBody.

memory.sources.extractionTextHelp.text: This is the text the extractor will read. Editing it does not change the chat's own summary.
memory.sources.extractionTextHelp.note: Help under the editable extraction text. The override is new to this console — upstream extraction always reads the source note verbatim — so nothing here can trace, and the second sentence is the one that stops a reviewer worrying they are editing the chat.

memory.sources.overrideNote.text: used the next time this source is extracted
memory.sources.overrideNote.note: Says when a saved extraction-text override takes effect, beside the save button. The catalog's sourceRefreshedRerunExtraction covers refreshing the imported text, which is the opposite direction.

memory.confirm.scope.note: Key in the import confirm's key/value body. The catalog's sourcesworkspace.importScope is the picker's own label and is too long for an 84px key column beside extraction and after. Lowercase because the key column uppercases in CSS.

memory.confirm.after.note: Key in the import confirm's key/value body, over the sentence describing what the import leaves behind. The catalog has no word for the aftermath of an action. Lowercase because the key column uppercases in CSS.

memory.report.kept.note: Column heading in the import report's per-source table. extractiondetails.kept is the same word welded to a comma ("kept,") for a run-on accounting line and cannot be used as a heading. Lowercase because the table head uppercases in CSS.

memory.restates.note: The claim repeats a line already stored — used as the queue's quick chip and as the eyebrow over the stored line in the detail. memory.flag.restatesVault is the flag's fuller noun phrase; this is the bare verb, which the catalog has nowhere because upstream filters near-duplicates out before review.

memory.sources.thisChat.note: Stands in for the scoped chat's name in the search-empty sentence when the chat has no name to show. The catalog has this verbatim; an earlier pass declined currentChat ("Current chat", a picker option that reads as a proper noun mid-sentence) but missed that thisChat is byte-identical to what we wanted.

memory.detail.retrieval.note: Heading over the one bordered block on the detail card. The catalog names the retrieval phase in the activity view; this is the same concept — whether the engine reaches this memory at all — over the fields that decide it.

memory.detail.retrievalWhat.note: Accessible name of the info button beside the retrieval heading. The catalog explains retrieval inside settings copy but never names a control that opens the explanation.

memory.detail.retrievalHelp.text: Keywords and modes decide whether the engine ever reaches this memory in a chat.
memory.detail.retrievalHelp.note: The retrieval popover's sentence, covering both fields in the block at once. longtermmemorydetail.underTheHoodKeywords explains how keyword matching works; this says what the block is FOR, and says it about modes as well.

memory.detail.modes.note: Key in the retrieval block's two-column grid. reviewqueue.modes is "Modes:" — the colon is part of the string, for a run-on readline — so it cannot be a grid label whose colon would read as a second separator. Lowercase to match the column.

memory.detail.sectionMeta.note: A section row's size read-out, in the same shape as memory.detail.moreLines and memory.detail.earlierLines. The product has no line-level view of stored text, so nothing upstream measures a section this way.

memory.detail.expandAll.note: The control that opens every section at once. memory.expand names one row's chevron; this acts on the whole set and carries a different glyph, so it must not borrow the row's word.

memory.detail.collapseAll.note: The counterpart to memory.detail.expandAll, and the card's manifest state: every section becomes a bare row. memory.collapse names one row's chevron.

memory.detail.keywordRail.note: Accessible name of the keyword rail, which is one tap target holding many keywords. The visible +N more counter is not a name, and the rail has to announce that tapping it does something.

memory.detail.flagWhy.note: Accessible name of a section row's flag button. The catalog has no per-section exception signal, so nothing upstream names the control that explains one.

memory.detail.sectionNearCap.note: A stored section approaching its cap. memory.flag.sectionNearCapNamed says the same of a PROJECTION over a review batch and ends "after this batch", which is false of a memory already sitting in the vault.

memory.detail.sectionOverCap.text: §{{key}} is at {{pct}}% of its {{cap}}-character cap and over the limit.
memory.detail.sectionOverCap.note: The far side of memory.detail.sectionNearCap for a stored section, ending in the console's own memory.overLimit phrase.

memory.detail.relationRelatedTo.note: The one link relation the catalog does not label. It ships relationExtractedFrom, relationOccurredIn, relationCausedBy and nine more in this exact sentence-case shape; related_to appears in stored payloads with no string beside it, so this fills the single gap in an otherwise complete set.

memory.detail.edited.note: The meta line's edit stamp. memoryvault.updated is the bare column heading "Updated"; this is the phrase in a running meta line, where the verb has to carry its timestamp.

memory.detail.version.note: The memory's version in the meta line, abbreviated because the line is mono data separated by ·. The catalog exposes a version only inside backup-validation prose.

memory.detail.edit.note: Opens the vault's editor from the read-only detail card. The catalog's own one-word Edit action.

memory.detail.sectionCount.note: How many sections the memory has, as the spoken name of the count beside the sections heading. The heading already renders the noun, so the visible figure stays bare and this carries the noun for a screen reader.

memory.vault.emptyAllArchived.note: The vault list emptied by archiving rather than by having nothing in it, in the same sentence shape as memory.vault.emptyScoped. The catalog never states this condition because upstream the vault lists archived memories, so it has no empty state they can cause. Deliberately states the condition and stops: the vault has no way to view archived memories yet, and naming a way out that does not exist is worse than naming none.

memory.vault.emptyScoped.text: No memories are available in this scope.
memory.vault.emptyScoped.note: The vault filtered to nothing by scope alone. The catalog ships this exact sentence shape for the two things it does scope — noLorebooksAreAvailableInThisScope, noSourcesHaveBeenImportedInThisScope — but never for saved memories, because upstream the vault is not a scoped view. Same sentence, right noun.

memory.vault.emptyScopedBody.text: Widening the scope will show memories from other characters and chats.
memory.vault.emptyScopedBody.note: Names the way out, as memory.sources.emptyScopedBody does for the sources list; that one says "import scope" and "sources", which is the wrong control and the wrong noun here. The catalog states the empty condition and never tells the reader that the scope is the thing to change.

memory.dock.droppedRequired.note: Heading of the apply sheet's dropped-dependency section. Preflight is sent only the keeps, so a dropped claim can only come back marked auto-included because a keep requires it. Short on purpose: the section heading is set in the label face, which is for structure and not for sentences, so the consequence lives in memory.dock.droppedRequiredWhy underneath it.

memory.dock.stillUndecided.note: The remainder of the queue as a sentence rather than a figure. memory.undecided is the bare decision state used on a row; this is a statement about how much work is left after Apply.

memory.dock.draftsStayOpen.note: A draft holding both a decided and an undecided claim is contacted and survives. Replaces memory.dock.stayPending, which said the same thing as a subjectless parenthetical hanging off a figure; standing on its own in a list of sentences it needs a subject. Upstream a draft is accepted whole, so the catalog cannot describe a partially-decided one.

memory.dock.editedStaged.one: {{count}} claim carries an edit you staged
memory.dock.editedStaged.note: Replaces memory.dock.editedCount ("{{count}} edited"), a fragment that only read as a label beside a value. The catalog counts edited mutations only to refuse them (invalidEditedMutation); it has no plain count of the ones that are fine.

memory.dock.droppedRequiredWhy.one: A claim you kept depends on it, but Apply honours the drop and leaves it out.
memory.dock.droppedRequiredWhy.other: Claims you kept depend on them, but Apply honours the drops and leaves them out.
memory.dock.droppedRequiredWhy.note: The consequence half of memory.dock.droppedRequired. Apply strips a dropped id back out even when preflight re-included it (model/tally.ts countReadyToSend), so the omission is stated rather than the addition. The catalog's dependency strings describe automatic inclusion succeeding and have no word for the ledger overruling it.

memory.dock.blockedWhy.one: The engine refused it. Apply sends everything else.
memory.dock.blockedWhy.other: The engine refused these. Apply sends everything else.
memory.dock.blockedWhy.note: The consequence half of memory.dock.blocked, which counts but does not say what becomes of them. Replaces memory.dock.blockedHeld ("{{count}} blocked — held back from Apply"), which welded count and outcome into one caps heading; the label face is for structure, not for a sentence with an em dash in it.

memory.dock.willFail.note: Heading of the section for the one structural failure preflight cannot see. Split out of memory.dock.droppedDependency, which carried count, cause and remedy in a single string and therefore had to be rendered as a caps heading two lines long.

memory.dock.willFailWhy.one: It depends on a create you dropped. Keep the create, or drop this too.
memory.dock.willFailWhy.other: They depend on a create you dropped. Keep the create, or drop them too.
memory.dock.willFailWhy.note: The cause and remedy half of memory.dock.willFail. The server auto-includes an undecided dependency but cannot recover one explicitly dropped, so this is the reviewer's to fix; the catalog's dependency strings describe automatic inclusion succeeding.
